nodes.summary: Call a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women disjoint if for every pair of positions $(r, s)$ there is exactly one man–woman pair in which the man ranks the woman at position $r$ and the woman ranks the man at position $s$. For every natural number $n$, the number of disjoint profiles is at most $(n^2)!$ and is divisible by $(n!)^2$.
nodes.title: Counting disjoint preference profiles

nodes.summary: Let $T$ and $T'$ be strict total orders on a set $\alpha$, with relations $\lt _T$ and $\lt _{T'}$. If $x \lt _T y \iff x \lt _{T'} y$ for all $x, y \in \alpha$, then $T = T'$.
nodes.title: Strict total orders are determined by their relation

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $W$ be finite sets with the same number of elements. Suppose that each $m \in M$ has a strict total order of preference on $W$ and each $w \in W$ has a strict total order of preference on $M$. Then some perfect matching between $M$ and $W$ is stable for these preferences.
nodes.title: Existence of stable perfect matchings

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $W$ be finite sets with the same number of elements. Suppose that each $m \in M$ has a strict total order of preference on $W$ and each $w \in W$ has a strict total order of preference on $M$. Then some perfect matching between $M$ and $W$ is stable for these preferences.
nodes.title: Gale–Shapley theorem

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women. The men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ ends in exactly one round if and only if every woman is the first choice of exactly one man.
nodes.title: When the Gale–Shapley algorithm ends in one round

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women in which all men rank the women in the same order. Then the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ ends in exactly $n$ rounds.
nodes.title: Gale–Shapley rounds when all men have the same preferences

nodes.summary: For the preference profile with no men and no women, the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm takes zero rounds.
nodes.title: Gale–Shapley rounds with no participants

nodes.summary: For a preference profile $P$ for $n$ men and $n$ women, the number of rounds of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ is the least $t$ such that every man is provisionally engaged after $t$ rounds (or $0$ if there is no such $t$).
nodes.title: Number of Gale–Shapley rounds

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women and let $t$ be a natural number. After $t + 1$ rounds of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$, a man who is provisionally engaged after $t$ rounds has made as many proposals as after $t$ rounds, and every other man has made one proposal more than after $t$ rounds.
nodes.title: One round of the Gale–Shapley algorithm

nodes.summary: For every preference profile, after zero rounds of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm every man has made zero proposals.
nodes.title: No proposals before the first round

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women. The number $p_t(i)$ of women man $i$ has proposed to after $t$ rounds of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ is defined by $p_0(i) = 0$ and, for every $t$, $p_{t+1}(i) = p_t(i)$ if man $i$ is provisionally engaged in the state $p_t$ and $p_{t+1}(i) = p_t(i) + 1$ otherwise: in each round every man who is not provisionally engaged proposes to his…
nodes.title: Proposal counts in the Gale–Shapley algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women, with positions in each ranking numbered $0, \dots, n - 1$, and consider the state of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm in which each man $i'$ has proposed to the women at the positions $r' < p(i')$ of his ranking. Man $i$ is provisionally engaged in this state if $1 \le p(i) \le n$ and the woman $w$ at his position $p(i) - 1$ (the last woman he…
nodes.title: Provisional engagement in the Gale–Shapley algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women and let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be stable matchings for $P$. If man $i$ and his wife $\mu(i)$ form a hell-couple in $\mu$ (each ranks the other last), then $\nu(i) = \mu(i)$.
nodes.title: A hell-couple belongs to every stable matching

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, and let $\mu$ be a stable matching for $P$, in which man $i$ marries woman $\mu(i)$. Then at most one man $i$ forms a hell-couple with his wife $\mu(i)$.
nodes.title: At most one hell-couple in a stable matching

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a strict total order on a set $\alpha$, with relation $\lt _T$. Then $a \lt _T a$ fails for every $a \in \alpha$.
nodes.title: Irreflexivity of a strict total order

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $W$ be sets. Suppose that each $m \in M$ has a strict total order $\lt _m$ of preference on $W$ and each $w \in W$ has a strict total order $\lt _w$ of preference on $M$, where $x \lt _m y$ means that $m$ prefers $x$ to $y$, and likewise for $\lt _w$. For a perfect matching $\mu$ between $M$ and $W$, a pair $(m, w) \in M \times W$ is a blocking pair when $w \lt _m \mu(m)$ and $m \lt _w \mu^{-1}(w)$,…
nodes.title: Blocking pair

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, and let $\mu$ be a matching in which man $i$ marries woman $\mu(i)$. Man $i$ and his wife $\mu(i)$ form a hell-couple when each ranks the other last: $i$ ranks $\mu(i)$ in his last position and $\mu(i)$ ranks $i$ in her last position.
nodes.title: Hell-couple

nodes.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, man $i$ and woman $j$ are soulmates when each ranks the other first: $j$ is the first choice of $i$ and $i$ is the first choice of $j$.
nodes.title: Soulmate pair

nodes.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, a matching $\mu$, in which man $i$ marries woman $\mu(i)$, is stable if and only if there are no man $i$ and woman $j$ such that $i$ ranks $j$ strictly above his wife $\mu(i)$ and $j$ ranks $i$ strictly above her husband $\mu^{-1}(j)$.
nodes.title: Stability in terms of ranks

nodes.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, a matching $\mu$, in which man $i$ marries woman $\mu(i)$, is stable when no man and woman both strictly prefer each other to their own spouses. Equivalently, $\mu$ is a stable perfect matching for the strict preferences induced by the men's and the women's rankings.
nodes.title: Stable matching

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $W$ be sets. Suppose that each $m \in M$ has a strict total order of preference on $W$ and each $w \in W$ has a strict total order of preference on $M$. A perfect matching $\mu$ between $M$ and $W$ is stable for these preferences when no pair $(m, w) \in M \times W$ is a blocking pair for $\mu$.
nodes.title: Stable perfect matching

nodes.summary: There is exactly one Latin square of order $0$, that is, $L_0 = 1$.
nodes.title: Latin squares of order zero

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $L_n$ is the number of Latin squares of order $n$: families $(M_0, \dots, M_{n-1})$ of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (the rows) such that for every position $r$ the entries $M_0(r), \dots, M_{n-1}(r)$ (column $r$) are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Number of Latin squares

nodes.summary: The relation of a strict total order $T$ on a set $\alpha$ is its underlying binary relation $\lt _T$ on $\alpha$, which is irreflexive, transitive, and relates any two distinct elements in one direction or the other.
nodes.title: Relation of a strict total order

nodes.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, each man $i$ gets the strict total order on the women in which $i$ prefers woman $a$ to woman $b$ exactly when he ranks $a$ at an earlier position than $b$.
nodes.title: Men's preferences induced by rankings

nodes.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, the rank of woman $j$ for man $i$ is the zero-based position $r \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ at which $i$ ranks $j$, so his favorite has rank $0$ and his least favorite has rank $n - 1$.
nodes.title: Rank of a woman for a man

nodes.summary: For all $n, k \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of preference profiles of $n$ men and $n$ women in which, for every position $r$, different men rank different women at position $r$ (the men's rankings form a Latin square), and which have exactly $k$ soulmate pairs, is
nodes.title: Profiles with Latin-square men's preferences, counted by soulmate pairs

nodes.summary: A binary relation $<$ on a set $\alpha$ that is irreflexive ($a \not< a$ for all $a$), transitive ($a < b$ and $b < c$ imply $a < c$) and total on distinct elements ($a \ne b$ implies $a < b$ or $b < a$) defines a strict total order on $\alpha$ whose relation is $<$.
nodes.title: Building a strict total order from a relation

nodes.summary: For sets $M$ (men) and $W$ (women), a preference profile of the men assigns to each $m \in M$ a strict total order on $W$, the preferences of $m$.
nodes.title: Men's preferences

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $L_n$ be the number of Latin squares of order $n$. Call the men's preferences of a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women Latin when, for every position $r$, distinct men rank distinct women at position $r$, and likewise for the women's preferences. The number of preference profiles whose men's and women's preferences are both Latin and that have exactly $k$ soulmate…
nodes.title: Mutually Latin profiles with $k$ soulmate pairs

nodes.summary: In a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women, a man $i$ and a woman $j$ form a pair of outcasts when every man other than $i$ ranks $j$ last and every woman other than $j$ ranks $i$ last. The number of preference profiles with at least one pair of outcasts is $14$ if $n = 2$ and $n^4 ((n-1)!)^{2n}$ if $n \ne 2$ (this is $0$ for $n = 0$).
nodes.title: Profiles with a pair of outcasts

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, where $n - k$ is read as $0$ when $k > n$. Consider the $n - k$ men $k, \dots, n - 1$ and the $n - k$ women $k, \dots, n - 1$ among $n$ men and $n$ women numbered from $0$, where each of these men ranks all $n$ women and each of these women ranks all $n$ men. The number of ways to choose these rankings so that no man and woman among them each rank the other first is
nodes.title: Outsiders without soulmate pairs

nodes.summary: A perfect matching between sets $M$ and $W$ is a bijection $\mu \colon M \to W$, which matches each $m \in M$ with $\mu(m) \in W$.
nodes.title: Perfect matching

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, number $n$ men and $n$ women by $0, \dots, n - 1$. A preference profile $P = (M, W)$ for them consists of a permutation $M_i$ of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ for each man $i$ and a permutation $W_j$ of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ for each woman $j$: $M_i(r)$ is the woman man $i$ ranks at zero-based position $r$, and $W_j(r)$ is the man woman $j$ ranks at position $r$.
nodes.title: Preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women

nodes.summary: Every preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women has at most $n$ soulmate pairs, since a man's soulmate is his first choice.
nodes.title: A profile has at most $n$ soulmate pairs

nodes.summary: The number of soulmate pairs of a preference profile $P$ for $n$ men and $n$ women is the number of pairs $(i, j)$ of a man $i$ and a woman $j$ that are soulmates in $P$, that is, each ranks the other first.
nodes.title: Number of soulmate pairs

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the number $F(k, n)$ of preference profiles for $n$ men and $n$ women with exactly $k$ soulmate pairs is
nodes.title: Number of profiles with exactly $k$ soulmate pairs

nodes.summary: A strict total order on a type $\alpha$ is a binary relation $<$ on $\alpha$ that is irreflexive ($a < a$ holds for no $a$), transitive ($a < b$ and $b < c$ imply $a < c$) and total on distinct elements ($a \ne b$ implies $a < b$ or $b < a$). In the Gale–Shapley development it models strict preference.
nodes.title: Strict preference order

nodes.summary: Let $<$ be the relation of a strict total order on a type $\alpha$. If $a, b \in \alpha$ and $a \ne b$, then $a < b$ or $b < a$.
nodes.title: Strict total orders are total on distinct elements

nodes.summary: Let $<$ be the relation of a strict total order on a type $\alpha$. If $a, b, c \in \alpha$ satisfy $a < b$ and $b < c$, then $a < c$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of a strict total order

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women with exactly $n - 1$ soulmate pairs (read as $0$ when $n = 0$). Then $P$ has exactly one stable matching. Moreover, for every stable matching $\mu$ of $P$ and every man $i$ who has no soulmate, the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ ends after $r + 1$ rounds, where $r$ is the zero-based position at which man $i$ ranks his wife $\mu(i)$.
nodes.title: Profiles with $n - 1$ soulmate pairs

nodes.summary: For a preference profile $P$ for $n$ men and $n$ women, each woman $j$ gets the strict total order on the men in which man $a$ comes before (is preferred to) man $b$ exactly when woman $j$ ranks $a$ at an earlier position than $b$.
nodes.title: Women's preference orders of a profile

nodes.summary: For a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women, the rank that woman $j$ gives man $i$ is the zero-based position at which she ranks him, that is, the paper's ranking minus one.
nodes.title: A woman's rank of a man

nodes.summary: For types $M$ and $W$, a preference profile of $W$ over $M$ assigns to each $w \in W$ a strict total order on $M$, read as the strict preference of $w$ among the elements of $M$.
nodes.title: Women's preference profile

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
